evidence_interpretation.positive_structural_evidence: The bounded audit found 115 distinct label-blind run candidates, matching the curator-declared count, and a consistent 54-item test-container shape for all 115 candidates.
evidence_interpretation.blocking_evidence: The same frozen audit detected protected label or supervision surface, extensive privacy or identifier surface, no nested notice closure, no v1/v2 overlap comparison, no global duplicate or independence proof, and no bound source-recoverable pointer.
evidence_interpretation.scientific_conclusion: LO2v2 has credible source-native run structure, but the reviewed index is not an evidence-safe model-visible surface. Structural capacity cannot override protected-label, privacy, notice, overlap, independence, or pointer Gates. It is unsuitable as the fourth train or development replacement family.

option_analysis.reason: The pre-registered label-isolation and privacy probes both failed. Those are hard source-role Gates and cannot be offset by valid JSON, 115 run candidates, consistent per-run container shape, or deterministic digests.

Changing the protected-label vocabulary after observing 6785 matches would be post hoc Gate manipulation. Attempts 1 through 3 are exhausted, and the frozen audit result must not be rescued by shrinking the detector.
Changing the privacy vocabulary after observing 219123 matches would reverse the frozen privacy contract and optimize the source to the Gate rather than establish an evidence-safe surface.

Post-result field, subtree, row, run, test, task, or status filtering could use protected identity or nuisance structure to manufacture a passing surface and would not close nested rights, global lineage, overlap, or pointer recovery.

The audit established distinct run-candidate tokens and one detected location per candidate, not completion uniqueness, reset boundaries, duplicate, retry, partial-run, repeated-system policy, or statistical independence.
The 54-item containers include protected test or task identity surface. Container count is not evidence-safe sample count and cannot receive sample or quota credit.
Only canonical in-memory construction was observed. Runtime log, metric, or trace binding and normalization-to-source recovery remain unverified, so binding_status must remain unbound.

A broader or dirtier surface cannot remediate protected-label and privacy failures in the narrow index. It would expand exposure and require an entirely new metadata, rights, acquisition, privacy, and audit authority.

The committed acquisition and sanitized aggregate audit may remain as auditable negative source-gate evidence. Any parser or fail-closed regression use requires separate authority and may not expose the local JSON to a model.

The fourth position must remain vacant until a distinct family passes immutable rights, protected-label, privacy, lineage, overlap, pointer, and nuisance-independence Gates without post hoc token changes or surface filtering.

Count tests, tasks, services, containers, metrics, traces, files, rows, timestamps, statuses, or the 54-item container shape as independent runs or evidence-safe samples.
Promote 115 distinct run candidates to globally unique completed executions or statistical independence without curator-backed reset, duplicate, retry, partial-run, and repeated-system policy.
Promote an in-memory digest or pointer candidate to a bound, source-recoverable, or model-visible pointer.
Use schema validity, curator count agreement, or deterministic digests to override label, privacy, notice, rights, overlap, lineage, pointer, or nuisance-independence Gates.
Download or open broader LO2v2 logs, metrics, traces, raw runtime archives, analysis packages, another revision, mirror, transformed table, or v1 artifact as automatic remediation.

reopen_conditions: The curator publishes a new immutable record revision with a physically separate privacy-safe, label-free manifest surface whose protected fields are absent upstream rather than filtered after this audit.

The new revision publishes machine-readable nested rights or notice metadata and a stable label-independent run manifest with completion, reset, duplicate, retry, partial-run, and repeated-system policy.
The new revision supports deterministic pointer recovery to the admissible source surface without exposing raw run, test, task, privacy, or identifier material.
A separately pinned v1 or protected comparison manifest becomes available so exact and near overlap can be evaluated without opening model-visible payload.
Any such revision must enter a new metadata candidate review and new acquisition and audit authorities. It is not a rerun or remediation of the rejected revision-4 index.
